answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks as a result finds them worthless when it returns to them. The glacier decay curve is applied at each close, karst records the drop, and jade recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 8 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. Every extra alias adds 2 hours of verification and 16 percent more locked value. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
